strengths: Well-motivated core insight that accuracy alone is insufficient for measuring learning difficulty; tree structure provides better information
Principled formalization of Reasoning Score (r-score) as maximum achievable accuracy gain under limited editing budget
Comprehensive experimental validation across 6 diverse math benchmarks with 7 baseline comparisons (GRPO, OPO, LPPO, Seed-GRPO, etc.)
Supporting analysis (MCN metric in Section 6.1, comparative evaluation in Section 6.2) validates core assumptions
Clear presentation with intuitive motivation (Figure 1) and well-structured method description (Figure 3)
Appropriate ablation studies on tree parameters (k, d) and weighting hyperparameters (ω_min, ω_max)
Reproducibility commitment with promised code and detailed experimental setup
weaknesses: Modest and inconsistent improvements (3.2% over ACC-based scheduling); concerning underperformance on Minerva Math for linear variant (36.4% vs 37.5% baseline); no statistical significance testing or error bars
Loose r-score definition: arbitrary M=4 budget never varied, 'non-conflicting nodes' vaguely defined, optimization complexity not discussed, potential NP-hardness unaddressed
Mismatch between r-score model (discrete node editing) and actual RL dynamics (continuous probability adjustment via gradients)

Crude tree approximation: fixed k-ary structure oversimplifies real reasoning; sparse l=200 token sampling may miss intermediate decisions; small ablation differences (48.3% vs 46.9%) suggest limited structural variance capture
Computational overhead of tree construction unanalyzed despite requiring ~k^d=256 trajectories per query; no wall-clock time or GPU memory comparisons
Limited scope: evaluation restricted to mathematical reasoning on 7B models with verifiable rewards; unclear generalization to other domains or model sizes
Incomplete validation: MCN computation method unclear, Figure 2 analysis is post-hoc (based on actual improvement, not prediction), M=4 chosen without ablation

Potential metric-weighting confound: Equations 9-10 nearly identical to accuracy-based scheduling (Equations 4-5); unclear whether gains come from r-score specifically or any alternative weighting; missing ablations comparing r-score to other structure-based metrics
Unexplored hyperparameter sensitivities: token interval l never varied, scheduling function γ(t) lacks justification, no sensitivity analysis for budget M
Missing recent comparisons (FastCURL not compared; Eurus-PRIME only on 7B Math)

strengths: Clear and compelling motivation: The q1/q2 example effectively illustrates why accuracy-based metrics are insufficient, and the distinction between 'concentrated' vs 'diffuse' error structures is insightful
Novel conceptual contribution: Framing RLVR as reasoning tree optimization and using tree structure for curriculum learning is principled and well-articulated
Comprehensive experimental validation: Evaluation across 6 diverse benchmarks with 2 model sizes, 7 baselines, and consistent improvements (up to 3.2% over ACC-based scheduling)
Strong validation of core claims: Section 6 provides compelling evidence that training optimizes tree structure (MCN decreasing) and r-score better identifies learnable queries than accuracy
Thorough experimental design: Ablation studies on tree parameters (k, d) and weighting hyperparameters, supplementary ablations, and reproducibility commitments
Practical relevance: Addresses an important problem in contemporary LLM training for math reasoning, a high-impact application domain
weaknesses: Moderate empirical gains with inconsistent benefits: Improvements range from 0.4-3.2% over strong baselines; 3% average gain over ACC-sigmoid may not justify added complexity for practitioners; variable benefits across benchmarks suggest method is task-dependent

Underspecified tree approximation: No analysis of how well k=4, d=4, l=200 captures actual reasoning structure; token interval l=200 appears arbitrary; no ablation on l; unclear robustness to approximation quality

Insufficient technical details on r-score computation: Equation (8) requires solving a combinatorial optimization problem (max subset sum with non-conflicting constraints) but the algorithm, computational complexity, and practical implementation are not explained; definition of 'non-conflicting' is vague

Weak theoretical justification: Why maximum accuracy gain under M-node budget is the right metric is not rigorously justified; limited connection to curriculum learning theory; 'node editing' metaphor oversimplifies actual policy gradient dynamics

Limited scope and generalizability: Only evaluated on math reasoning with verifiable integer answers; applicability to other reasoning domains, open-ended generation, or tasks without clear correctness signals is unclear

Missing computational cost analysis: No timing measurements or wall-clock time comparison despite expensive tree construction (k^d = 256 samples per query × 17K queries); practitioners cannot assess practical utility

Incomplete baseline comparisons: ACC-based curriculum is relatively simple; Seed-GRPO and LPPO show mixed results; established curriculum learning methods from broader ML literature not compared; no comparison with entropy-driven methods (Wang et al. 2025)

Hyperparameter proliferation and overfitting risk: Method introduces many hyperparameters (k, d, l, M, ωmin, ωmax, γ(t)); limited ablation on l and M; no ablation on scheduling function (linear vs sigmoid); risk of overfitting to validation set
Lack of per-benchmark analysis: High variance across benchmarks (e.g., +3.8% on Minerva but +1.1% on AMC23) not explained; no systematic analysis of when/why method works; no failure case analysis

strengths: Novel reasoning tree-based difficulty metric that captures structural complexity rather than just accuracy, with clear motivation and compelling examples

Comprehensive experimental validation across 6 benchmarks with consistent improvements (up to 3.2%), thorough ablation studies, and additional generalization tests (code generation, multiple architectures)
Strong analytical validation that training optimizes reasoning trees (Section 6.1, MCN metric) and that r-score better identifies learnable queries than accuracy (Section 6.2)
Technically solid formulation with formal definitions (Eq. 7-8) grounding scheduling in tree-based optimization rather than ad-hoc metrics
Well-executed experimental work with reproducibility support (code availability, detailed setup), variance analysis, and practical engineering optimizations (KV-Cache)
weaknesses: Critical algorithmic detail missing: How is the combinatorial optimization in Eq. (8) solved? No discussion of computational complexity or algorithm choice (exact vs. greedy vs. approximate)

Approximation quality not validated: Fixed k-ary trees are crude approximations of true solution spaces; no analysis of how well they represent actual reasoning structure or comparison with alternative approximations beyond limited ablations

Significant theoretical gap: r-score assumes discrete node edits with fixed budgets, but RL training uses continuous gradients affecting multiple nodes simultaneously; no justification for correlation between structural simplicity and gradient-based learning difficulty

Substantial computational overhead: Default configuration adds 48.54% cost, better configurations exceed 170%; while claimed manageable, this may limit practical adoption and trade-offs are not analyzed

Limited scope and generalization: Primary evaluation on mathematical reasoning (5/6 benchmarks); code generation improvements are marginal (+0.9-2.4%); applicability beyond verifiable-reward reasoning domains unclear
Modest empirical gains: 3.2% improvement over baselines is solid but not dramatic; only variance reported, not formal significance testing; improvements could vary significantly across benchmarks

Incomplete technical exposition: 'Conflicting nodes' definition in Eq. (8) needs formalization; token interval robustness shows non-monotonic behavior (Table 9) unexplained; dynamic r-score offers no benefit (Table 14), suggesting static metric misses important learning dynamics
Design choice justification lacking: Budget M=10, weights (0.5, 2.0), and token interval l=200 appear somewhat arbitrary; why deeper trees consistently outperform shallower ones deserves analysis
